name: OpenVibe.Run

exposure.note: openvibe.run serves its own front page, legal pages and sitemap (Run#28, 2026-10-11); the jobs API answers under /api/v1.

liveness.means: the process is up and answers HTTP; the database, Events and Bot are what ready checks

drains: dispatcher poller stopped (no new tick; the one in flight finishes)
job event streams closed (a client reconnects)

resumes.what: every job and its frames are committed rows: the first poller tick after boot places queued jobs, mirrors placed and running ones from Bot, and expires those past their ttl
run.job.* events and usage readings written before the stop wait in their outboxes and are relayed at boot

conditions: automatic: ovhost deploy puts the previous sha back and restarts again when the ready URL does not answer 2xx within ready.timeoutSeconds after the restart (exit 3)
rollback.window: automatic only while ovhost waits for readiness after the restart; manual afterwards, as long as no blocker applies

blockers.none: migrations 0001-0004 are expand-only (Run's own job, usage outbox and telemetry tables): an older release runs on the newer schema

leases.none: no claims: one process places jobs, one poller tick at a time; a job moves on by conditional row updates in Run's own database

notes: The job service of the network (plan T14, ADR-034): accepts jobs (run.job-create-request@1), places each on a node that advertises worker:<class> (platform.resource-offer@1, platform.runtime-offer@1, platform.workload-requirements@1), sends it as platform.job@1 over the node link and follows its platform.job-frame@1 frames. Consumes billing.usage.record to write one usage reading per wall-clock second (run:<job id>:<n>, service run, operation function.invoke, unit s) and media.object.read to resolve digest-pinned inputs. Serves its job API on loopback :4920 (Run #1 and #2, 2026-10-07).

site.name: Compute
site.tagline: Run jobs on machines that can.
site.what: Send a job to one API with your project's token: Compute places it on a node that offers its runtime, streams its output and meters it per second.
site.description: OpenVibe.Run executes jobs: a project submits a job (a pre-registered artifact, its input and its limits) to one API, Run chooses a node from the network's offers that its requirements allow, OpenVibe.Bot hands it to the node and meters every wall-clock second, the output streams back, and the job ends succeeded, failed, cancelled or expired. Alpha: jobs run on nodes paired with OpenVibe through the OpenVibe Node.

pillars.title: One API
pillars.text: Submit, read, list, cancel and stream jobs over HTTP, with RFC 9457 problems for every refusal.

pillars.title: Placed, not guessed
pillars.text: Each job goes to a node whose offer meets its requirements; the placement records the node, provider and region.

pillars.title: Live output
pillars.text: A short-lived ticket opens the job's event stream: state changes and the node's output as they happen.

pillars.title: Metered per second
pillars.text: The node link measures each job's wall clock; that reading is what the job is charged against.

faq.question: What does OpenVibe.Run do?
faq.answer: It runs jobs: a project submits a job (a registered artifact, its input and its limits), and Run places it on a node whose offer meets its requirements.

faq.question: Where do jobs run?
faq.answer: On nodes paired with OpenVibe through the OpenVibe Node, including computers of your own.

faq.question: How is a job charged?
faq.answer: By the wall-clock seconds the node measures for it.

faq.question: Can I watch a job run?
faq.answer: Yes. Its event stream shows each state change and the node's output as it happens.

site.keywords: openvibe run, job runner, run jobs on nodes, sandbox api, per-second metering
